verdict.rationale: Figma exposes webhooks that let external systems 'listen for events' (comments, version updates, library changes) which can be wired to trigger custom actions, and plugins/widgets can execute logic when invoked — but Figma itself provides no native rules engine or built-in 'if event then action' automation surface; the actual triggering logic must be built externally via webhook consumers or custom plugins. Missing for 10: a first-party rules/automation builder inside Figma, evidence of built-in conditional action execution, and any hands-on confirmation that webhook-driven automations work reliably end-to-end.
